Objective for processing:  Use of data for ensuring service delivery in various hospitals throughout England is matching local service levels, ensuring quality of service is comparable at a local and national level, to provide assurances against 'cherry picking'. 
Ramsay Health Care currently has 31 Acute hospitals and treatment centres providing elective NHS outpatient and admitted care services, throughout England. These services cover a variety of specialties and are primarily commissioned through Standard Contracts. In addition, they also undertake specifically commissioned subcontracted activity from other providers, such as NHS Trusts and other Independent Health Care providers. All of their hospitals list their services on Choose and Book, and they also receive referrals through local triage hubs, direct paper referrals and transfer lists. 
In addition to ensuring that Ramsay Health Care are providing the best and most appropriate services (specialties and treatments) at each of their hospitals, according to the local health economy requirements, they also need to be able to examine, and if necessary prove, that the services they are providing are a suitable mix and spread of complexity in each resource group to counter any potential claim that they are selective of the patients and treatments they provide – ‘Cherry-picking’.
Due to the applicant’s hospitals covering such a large geographic area around England, it means they receive commissioned activity from almost every commissioner in England, in all the PHE regions, as well as NHS England commissioned activities into the hospitals. For this reason, the applicant requires the entire datasets requested in order to perform benchmarking and analysis.
Ramsay Health Care intends to process the extracts to drive analysis and benchmarking in the following areas:
1.	Coding practice at a National and Local level, comparing independent sector coding depth with NHS provider coding depth.  In addition the applicant will be looking at the distribution procedures by provider and commissioner. This will support insight into the accuracy of Ramsay coding and identify areas for improvement in the coding of future activity thereby facilitating more accurate data submissions of activity performed
2.	Analysing Length of Stay and re-admissions by procedure, consultant and provider contextualised with complexity taken from ICD information in order to identify areas for improvement and subsequent enhancements to patient quality outcomes
3.	The measurement of specific services provided by Ramsay’s Hospitals, along with specific procedures by volume, length of stay, complexity and various other combinations of fields that may be required to give context and a deeper understanding of local and National trends. Ramsay Health Care intends to benchmark their performance with other Independent and NHS providers in an effort to further drive better efficiency and patient experience.
Ramsay Health Care will be looking at a lot of variables (31 hospitals in different locations throughout England, multiple specialties at each hospital location, multiple clinicians for each service and multiple outcomes there-in – all of which will be compared to local and national benchmark data provided by the analysis) so there is considerable potential for recognising areas of development and improvement.

Processing activities: 
Ramsay Health Care will be benchmarking their own provider data, sourced from their Patient Administration System (PAS) and associated systems, with the wider HES dataset. All data processing will be performed internally and outputs will be re-aggregated for localised management information purposes by Hospital managers and local and national clinical teams. No data will be passed to any external third parties, and any internal requests for activity level data to provide clarification on the aggregated data will be handled directly by the head office data analysts under the direction of the Ramsay Health Care Information Governance Officer.
With regards to data mapping, there will be no re-identifying of patients for any purpose. Ramsay Health Care will only be mapping aggregated data samples to their own locally derived (also aggregated) datasets. The requirement for non-aggregated, detailed datasets is for analysing coding differences by HRG (Health Resource Group), specialty, location and commissioner to aid localised benchmarking and won’t be analysed on a patient-level basis.
The offices in Bedford are an administrative head office, and this is where the IT department is based. Consequently, the HES data will be stored on a dedicated SQL2005 server at this location. However, the Information Services team are based in the London Executive office, and this is where the data will be used. Technically, the processing will be taking place on the dedicated server in Bedford, since it is the computer doing the processing, however the human operators will be based in London, and this is where the outputs will be analysed. Access will only be over the secure and protected internal network, and there are stringent role based access policies in operation.
All data processing and analysis will take place internally by a small team of employed data analysts. The data will be analysed using SQL Server analysis tools directly interacting with the database, thereby avoiding the need to return activity level data to applications such as spreadsheets, and once the sensitive level data has been mapped, any resulting outputs will be aggregated to the necessary level for the purposes of sharing the results. 
The applicant intends to process the extracts to drive analysis and benchmarking in the following areas:
1.	Coding practice at a National and Local level analysis will be achieved with a patient level extract including diagnostic and procedure information that will enable the applicant to perform statistical analysis on the dataset.
2.	Analysing Length of Stay and re-admissions will necessitate the creation of an extract containing diagnostic and procedure information, along with consultant, length of stay, admission method, discharge destination, relevant patient demographics (such as age, gender and ethnicity) and procedure setting (Daycase or Inpatient). Having built this extract the applicant will then perform statistical analysis on the dataset to determine correlation and significance.
3.	The applicant intends to measure specific services (e.g. Orthopaedics) at individual Ramsay Units and specific procedures (such as Hip Replacements) against other providers.  To achieve this the applicant will build an extract detailing the volume, length of stay, complexity and other relevant fields to benchmark their clinical performance against other Independent Sector Providers and NHS providers
Ramsay Health Care understand that further analysis and use of the data sets beyond that set out above will require them to submit an amendment application prior to analysis starting.

Specific outputs expected, including target date: 
Headline summaries of outputs will be provided to Hospital Managers, clinical teams, service development managers and Senior Executive teams and individual Consultants, all of which are fully employed or contracted to Ramsay Health Care.  These ‘output recipients’ will not have access to the core data – it will be the responsibility of the data processor to produce focused reports, relevant to individual and groups of recipients. The data processor will employ standard statistical techniques when processing, visualising and presenting the results which will include, where relevant, topping and tailing the data to remove statistical outliers. Small numbers will be suppressed in line with the HES analysis guide.
Intended indicators will measure specific services and outcomes (for example, Hip replacements) in terms of volumes, length of stay, complexity, etc. and compare this data with other providers, locally and nationally, to ensure that the organisation is providing equal or superior treatment to other providers, as well as a comparable complexity and variety, to drive better efficiency and patient experience. 
In addition, the Organisation will be able to provide information to their clinical teams, consultants, management and commissioner liaison teams about areas for development or improvement. This will be communicated through internal presentations and standard business communications, or through collaborative internal conferences.

Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: 
This data will not be used in any direct communications, but the results of the analysis will provide better information and communication deliverables with commissioners, GP's and other key suppliers.  Communication deliverables are defined by the sharing of aggregated, relevant performance outcomes derived from HES data. This will NOT include things like pamphlets, posters or other marketing materials and will be communicated directly in writing. By benchmarking Ramsay data against other comparable providers, areas for improvement in terms of clinical performance and data quality can be identified. Ramsay Health Care will be comparing their performance to organisations providing similar services and communicating this comparison to NHS commissioners and that data will not be used to market services outside of sharing this comparison with NHS commissioners. Where such differences are significant they will be reviewed and potential reasons for variances will be explored before plans for rectification are considered and developed. Once implemented, such plans should ultimately result in the delivery of improved services to patients, thereby benefiting the wider healthcare economies and patient quality metrics.
